lastReleaseMessage: The artist's rubble and roads reach the map. Every wall joint is proved in play. The gate brief for her next round is written. Her four rubble pieces are blocking scenes on the decor base: a piece claims its footprint in the grid's occupancy, so units path around it, the navmesh bakes it out and nothing builds on it. A mission layout shape whose tile is rubble fills with them; a mission's rubble_density scatters them. Her four road slabs are the sources of a road tileset. An authored Roads tile layer draws it, two tiles to a cell, and a layout stroke whose tile is road paints it. Give Ground paints the road its brief describes. Old Ground paints the same road and leaves rubble where its ruined wall ends, so its fingerprint is re-recorded on purpose. tools/navy_drop_check.gd builds all sixteen wall joint masks in Skirmish and names the clip each wall plays. docs/GATES-2026-10-19.md is the brief for her gate round. Whether rubble can ever be cleared is D-OPEN-60. The screen-tree gate now measures the settings screen against default options instead of the machine's saved file, which a moved volume slider had changed.

items: Record pages ship visible = false because no mechanic recovers them. Every campaign mission carries a record_page_id and an optional RECOVER_OBJECT objective, and nothing in the game can satisfy one.
DONE 2026-09-23: the six full-screen menus, the end-of-mission overlay, the loading overlay, the tutorial prompt and the Test Arena bar are authored scenes; scripts build only data-driven rows.
DONE 2026-09-23: fog of war, the minimap and the wave director are authored in gameplay.tscn behind resize_to_grid and refresh_from_grid hooks the controller calls once the mission settles the grid.

DONE 2026-09-23: the research tree (28) and the Keeper catalogue (80) are .tres Resources behind two manifests. The wave schedule defaults, the train recipes, the trade recipes, every building cost: all moved to Resources or scene data alongside.

Mortend Bold, the typeface the main menu logo was rendered in, is licensed for personal use only (assets/fonts/LICENSES.md, 2026-10-19). Before any sold build: buy the Arterfak Project commercial license, or re-render the logo in a font under free terms.

Gate rebuild on the wall system when the gate rig lands: a gate is a wall tile with a friendly-passable edge on its axis, two flanking wall cells placed with it, doors that open for a nearby friendly and never for the horde. The O hotkey and the two-halves house stand-in go with it. She draws the rig against docs/GATES-2026-10-19.md.

Quarry rework with the artist. The v0.62.0 build places a Quarry on its deposit because her rig draws the worked site over the deposit; the owner ruled on 2026-09-14 that this is not the Quarry he wants, and that the rework is low priority. The on-deposit build stays as the interim until then.

One enemy path, step 1 of 4: flow field toward the colony replaces the single-waypoint beeline in enemy_pool._set_path_to_node. Sampled O(1) per record and rebuilt when buildings change, which already triggers a navmesh rebake. Walls stay out of the field exactly as they stay out of the navmesh (building.gd), so the wall redirect stays the physical layer. Port the per-enemy target offset from enemy_base._push_target_to_agent so the horde does not conga.

One enemy path, step 2 of 4: port dormancy (wake, re-sleep, idle wander) from enemy_dormancy.gd onto EnemyData. Split EnemyData.last_stim_time FIRST: it is documented as the re-sleep cooldown but enemy_pool reuses it as the target-reacquire timer, so porting re-sleep onto that field breaks reacquisition silently. investigating_noise and noise_target_tile already sit on the record unread.

One enemy path, step 3 of 4: move the 150 standing world Shamblers from mission_setup.gd (direct shambler.tscn instantiate, no pool routing, no flag check) onto enemy_pool.spawn_shambler with is_dormant set. Gated on the dormancy port or they lose their noise wake.

One enemy path, step 4 of 4: delete enemy_base.gd, the eight per-type enemy scripts and scenes, the eight use_multimesh_* flags, the wave_director routing branch, and enemy_anim.gd. Confirm debug_spawns.gd and trench_sweeper.gd first.

Noise pulls ACTIVE enemies, not only dormant ones (Kane's call 2026-08-26). New behavior, not a port: _investigating_noise is set in exactly two places, both inside the dormant branches of enemy_dormancy.gd, so an enemy already hunting never begins investigating. Needs a threshold well above sustained rifle fire at the wall, or it either does nothing visible or drags waves off the wall and hands the player a trivial counter to Hold the Wall.

Seven of the eight pooled enemy types render a frozen single frame; only the Shambler has a baked sheet. The per-Node scripts for Shoaling, Brinecaster and Leviathan loaded the Shambler placeholder until 2026-10-19; each now preloads its own art, seated on its measured content bottom.

The Numbers tab gives it 20 Food + 30 Gold and 60 s and says it is not yet Barracks-trainable; the unit scene, its static sprite and its portrait exist, and a TrainRecipe resource is a one-file add. Combined-load frame time: 400 enemies plus 40 units runs at a 32.46 ms median against the 16.67 ms budget, with a 95th percentile of 95.71, on the debug binary. DONE 2026-10-02: the baked unit path is the cheap one. Forced on its own and drawn, a baked unit costs 0.08 to 0.10 ms with no extra draw call, a live rig 0.37 to 0.55 ms with 43, so LIVE_RIG_BUDGET stays at 8 (scale-architecture-07, performance-09).

The per-unit target scan is the biggest single lever at the combined load: switching it off took the combined case from 32.46 to 22.56 ms, more than half the overage (scale-architecture-07). A spatial index or a scan cadence is the shape of the fix.

The history is measured and recorded: 424.93 MiB packed across 5,225 objects, against the 15.6 MB working tree the decision had been resting on. What it is made of settles the question rather than reopening it. Summing every blob version by path, docs/GDD.html accounts for 249.6 MB and CHANGELOG.md for 52.2 MB, two text documents rewritten in full on each of 344 releases, while the largest art file in the whole history is 6.8 MB. Roughly three quarters of the weight is text that large-file storage does not address. The decline stands and its first reason is stronger: rewriting 425 MiB of history on a repository with a live remote is a worse trade than it looked. The record also names the clone-size problem as a different job with different tools.

post-audit-digests.ps1 names #rising-audit, which is the channel its webhook is bound to. It printed #rising-resources, and the handler's own table records that the Resources webhook was never created.

Settled on #rising-backlog, and the two backlog scripts plus the release header are corrected to it. The handler's table won because it is the side that was checked against Discord and records which webhook is not created; the scripts carried a name copied from a sibling project whose category is shaped differently. The handler now says which side won and why. Only the printed string was ever affected, since routing follows the webhook file.

diagnose-gdd-publish.ps1 reads the live GATED_DOCS entry instead of the static file the key-value migration retired, which is why it reported MISSING on every run. It prints the live byte count, the live hash and the local hash of docs/GDD.html, and says DRIFT with both sizes when they disagree. Hash as well as size, because a publish that truncated or re-encoded the document keeps its length more often than not.

The gauntlet runs once per release. release.ps1 sets BR_PRESHIP_DONE after its own passing run, and the pre-commit hook stands down when it sees it. The direct call stays and the hook is the one that yields, because the hook lives under .git/ and is untracked: it can be missing on a fresh clone, and a release must not depend on a file that may not be there. The variable is set only for that process and its children, so a bare commit from any other shell still meets the whole wall, and a release that dies before committing takes the variable with it. push-to-github.ps1 also rewrites a hook that predates the change, since an untracked old copy would otherwise keep running the gauntlet twice on every machine that already had one.

Measured, then throttled. tools/bench_scale.gd gained a roaming case that keeps the whole roster walking for the sample window, plus a no-fog twin of it so the stamp could be attributed rather than guessed at. Forty units walking cost 32.89 ms over baseline with the fog on and 8.64 ms with it off, putting the stamp at 24.25 ms, or 0.61 ms per moving unit per frame against a 16.67 ms frame. The re-stamp threshold went from one pixel, which meant every frame for anything walking, to a quarter tile read off constants.TILE_W, which is the distance at which the low-resolution explored texture actually changes. Re-measured after: the roaming case fell from 32.89 ms to 8.90 ms against its no-fog twin at 8.18 ms, so the stamp now costs 0.72 ms for forty moving units, and the stationary case improved from 14.20 ms to 9.37 ms as well.

The changelog tab has the search box, a bump filter and the shown-count the backlog and asset tabs already had. The entries are text separated by line breaks rather than elements, so the filter wraps each one in a span the first time it runs and filters spans after that, which keeps a 344-entry list responsive. Verified in a browser: 344 shown at rest, 1 for a phrase search that returned the right entry, 70 for the minor filter, and 344 again on clear.

skirmish.tres is called Skirmish in the play menu and every save slot, and its briefing describes the mode rather than the art preview it stopped being: one Lantern, one map, no campaign orders, and a seed that replays the same ground.

save_load.gd gained _tile_in_bounds, and both _recreate_building and _recreate_unit refuse a saved tile that falls outside the live grid, warning with the class and the tile. Refuse rather than clamp: clamping stacks every out-of-bounds entity on one edge tile, which reads as a wall the player never built and is harder to explain than one that is missing, and the caller already reports a refusal the way it reports a missing scene. A grid that cannot say how big it is gets the benefit of the doubt, since the guard exists to catch a mismatch rather than to refuse a load. Nine checks in run_tests.gd cover the corners, the negatives, the unsized grid and the null grid; shipped in v0.70.0 with 1983 tests passing.
